text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Air France chairman Christian Blanc in an interview defends his view of buying both Airbus and Boeing aircraft, instead of only European Airbus as the government would prefer.
-- State sells a 10 percent stake in oil group Elf Aquitaine held through holding Erap for 10 billion francs. Funds to be used to recapitalise state-owned firms.
LA TRIBUNE DESFOSSES
-- Health Minister Jacques Barrot rules out a proposal by Axa chairman Claude Bebear of setting up a private social security system alongside the current mandatory system.

-- State-owned telecommunications operator France Telecom considers buying stake in Luxemburg satellite, thus giving up project of developing own satellite system. France Telecom spokesman denies discussions taking place.
-- Insurer GAN to inject some 800 million francs in ailing subsidiary UIC.
-- European new car registrations were up 14.6 percent in October.
-- New 500-million-franc yearly tax on meat to finance disposal of cattle by-products as part of plan to eradicate BSE "mad cow" disease.
L'AGEFI
-- Merrill Lynch plans to open investment banking operations in Paris in 1997.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Renault and PSA PEUP.P carmakers seek to rejuvenate workforce to gain competitiveness, consider job cuts and hiring younger workers.
-- CGT union leader Louis Viannet calls for further action against Prime Minister alain Juppe's policy and notably planned social security reforms.
LIBERATION (Economic section)

-- Planned 1996 deficit to remain unchanged at 288 billion francs and four percent of GDP, despite a spending increase of 40 billion francs, budget minister Alain Lamassoure said as he presented the mini-budget yesterday.
-- Paris area public transports to strike tomorrow for employment, wages and safety.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Renault and Peugeot downsizing plan could burden France as it attacks deficit.
